chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Al-Halabi, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

A man asked me about a woman who died and had not performed Hajj, and she bequeathed [money] to be used for Hajj. I was asked about it: if it was more preferable that it be placed among the poor of the offspring of Fatimah, it was placed among them; and if Hajj was more preferable, Hajj was performed for her. So I said to him: If an obligatory Hajj was due upon her, then spending what she bequeathed on Hajj is more beloved to me than distributing it in other than that.
ai.seo_question: What is the preferred use of a bequest for Hajj if the deceased woman owed an obligatory Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Shia juristic principle of 'al-ashlah' (choosing the more beneficial option) when executing a bequest for Hajj. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between the obligatory Hajj, which takes precedence, and the discretionary use of funds, allowing for distribution to the 'poor of the children of Fatima' if that yields greater spiritual or social benefit. This reflects the broader Shia emphasis on the Ahl al-Bayt's lineage as a primary recipient of charity and the flexibility in fulfilling religious duties based on contextual wisdom.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hamaad Bin Usman, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘A man asked me<sup>asws</sup> about a woman who died and had not performed Hajj. So she bequeathed, and he looked at an amount with which Hajj could be performed with. So he asked about it, if it was more favourable that he places it among the poor of the Children of Syeda Fatima<sup>asws</sup>, so he would place it among them, and if it was that the Hajj was more favourable, he would perform Hajj with it. So I<sup>asws</sup> said to him: ‘If the Obligatory Hajj was upon her, so spending what she has bequeathed with regarding the Hajj is more beloved to me than distribution in other than that’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad ibn ‘Uthaman from al-Halabiy who has narrated the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

A man once asked me about a woman who died without performing al-Hajj but made a will about an amount which is sufficient for al-Hajj. He asked if it is better to spend it on the needy people from the descendents of Fatimah, ‘Alayha al-Salam, it will be done so; if performing al-Hajj is better al-Hajj would be performed for her. I said to him that if al-Hajj was obligatory on her, spending it for al-Hajj is more beloved to me than distributing on other things.’”
